To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the MSY reference point is not a good metric to implement the EU CFP reform, 2) logMSY, a new reference point that we have proposed, is a better metric to achieve the goals of the EU CFP and 3) optimal harvesting control rules based on logMSY can be used to achieve the EU CFP goals.

the European Union should consider the following points for the CFP reforms:
    - The European Union should consider a reference point that is not the MSY.

1) if MSY is the reference point, optimal control rules may imply pulse fishing, which would not be accepted by the stakeholders; 2) logMSY may be a more appropriate reference point for the implementation of optimal control rules, and 3) optimal control rules that stabilize biomass and employment around the optimal stationary levels are more socially desirable and politically feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the implementation of the CFP, based on the logMSY and optimal harvesting control rule.
the implementation of the CFP, in the light of the new European Union’s fisheries policy, which will be adopted by the European Parliament in 2013.
the implementation of the MSY concept in fisheries.

the logMSY is a more appropriate metric for the implementation of CFP than the MSY.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a reform of the CFP based on the logMSY as reference point and optimal harvesting control that stabilize the employment around the optimal stationary value, would be more efficient and socially acceptable than a reform based on the MSY as reference point.
the CFP should be based on the concept of logMSY, which is more robust than MSY, and that optimal management should be based on optimal control theory.

the CFP reform should not be restricted to the use of the MSY as reference point, but it should also consider other metrics and optimal control rules that are able to stabilize the fishing effort and the biomass at the optimal values.
